note: Reversal can turn refusal into agreement or conceal discomfort. The cream example could concern treatment; the music example could invalidate a sensory boundary. Consequences depend on context, but an explicit negative must survive.

A bandage question becoming a factual claim can falsely reassure a listener. A statement becoming an instruction changes the interaction. Require confirmation; urgency and the consequence of acting make severity vary.
Changing who emails or who was told creates false commitments and responsibility. Confirm the actor before speech; medication, consent or legal contexts could make this critical.

Removing maybe from losing a card converts a possibility into a claim that could trigger action. Added uncertainty can also weaken an intended statement. The filters example additionally needs clarification of the action.

Voice and interpersonal stance belong to the speaker. Adding please can weaken a boundary, while dropping it can change an intended relationship signal. Usually less hazardous than negation reversal, but explicit choices still require protection.

A completed confirmation is different from a current one; a past report is not a current request for a report. Incorrect chronology can misdirect care or obligations. Verify the event time rather than attaching past to a noun.

Invented reporting events attribute knowledge, instructions or responsibility that was never selected. The assignment example can reverse who was to send it. Block automatic speech pending confirmation when invented content is consequential.
